The cheapest way to use Seedance 2.5

Edited by Emmanuel Gonzalez

Some links on this page are affiliate links. Affiliate disclosure.

The cheapest published Seedance 2.5 rate in the catalog today is $0.103/s on Replicate (480p, non_video_in), checked Nov 13, 2026 PT. That figure is a published rate for output video with no video input. Credit-plan rates below assume every paid credit is used in full. Unlimited windows have time, clip, and resolution caps; they are not treated as $0/s. Affiliate links never change this price order.

Last checked 2026-11-13.

What is the cheapest way to use Seedance 2.5?

The cheapest published rate in the catalog is $0.103/s on Replicate (480p, non_video_in), checked Nov 13, 2026 PT on the official model page. Credit-plan dollars per second assume every paid credit is used. A live unlimited window can cost less per second only after you generate more than the break-even seconds against the cheapest same-resolution catalog API, and only inside its caps. Unused credits, failed generations, minimum charges, and token-billing variance all raise the real rate.

What is the cheapest option at 480p, 720p, and 1080p?

At 480p, the lowest catalog rate is $0.103/s on Replicate (pay-as-you-go API, 480p, non_video_in), checked Nov 13, 2026 PT. At 720p, the lowest catalog rate is $0.231/s on Replicate (pay-as-you-go API, 720p, non_video_in), checked Nov 13, 2026 PT. At 1080p, the lowest catalog rate is $0.591/s on Atlas Cloud (API estimate, 1080p, Seedance 2.5 T2V), checked Nov 12, 2026 PT. Higgsfield API also publishes a list price from $0.118/s for five modes up to 1080p; the list does not state the resolution of the cheapest mode.

Hidden costs

Failed generations

The vendor pages checked today do not state a single, clear refund or no-charge policy for failed Seedance 2.5 generations. Treat that cost as unknown. A failed job that still bills raises every rate below.

Runway minimum and input video

Runway bills seedance2_5 at 20 / 30 / 68 credits per second of output at 480p / 720p / 1080p, plus 10 / 15 / 34 credits per second of input and reference video, with an 80 credit minimum per generation. Credits are $0.01 each, so the minimum is $0.80 before any output length, and a short clip with input video costs more than the catalog output-only rate. A preview (draft: true) bills at the 480p rate; enhancing that preview to 1080p is a second, separate 1080p charge. Sales tax may apply. (Runway API pricing, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT).

Magnific credits expire

Magnific annual plans grant credits per year (“Credits valid for 1 year, no monthly resets”). The catalog $/s figures assume those credits are used in full. Leftover credits raise the effective rate. Prices exclude VAT and local taxes. The page says you can top up credits anytime; it does not state a minimum top-up on the pricing page checked today. (Magnific pricing, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT).

fal and Atlas token billing

fal publishes roughly $0.2205 / $0.4730 / $1.164 per second at 480p / 720p / 1080p, billed by tokens. The token count is a function of output size, duration, and (for some endpoints) input video duration, so the invoice can differ from the per-second estimate (fal Seedance 2.5, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT). Atlas labels its listed rates “(estimated)” and says the final charge uses actual completion tokens after the task finishes. Reference-to-video requests that include a reference video are billed on output plus reference-video tokens (Atlas Cloud pricing, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT).

Higgsfield API funds and list price

Higgsfield API's Seedance 2.5 list price is “from” $0.118/s. Concurrent generation limits count only funds added in the past 28 days. The pricing page checked today does not state a minimum top-up or a failed-generation refund rule. (Higgsfield API pricing, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT).

What is confirmed, and what is not

Confirmed today (Nov 12, 2026 PT) on the vendors' own pages, and matching the catalog rows used above: Replicate's four published per-second rates of $0.1028 (non_video_in, 480p), $0.4304 (video_in, 480p), $0.2312 (non_video_in, 720p), and $0.9676 (video_in, 720p), which the tables show with the site's usual rounding; Higgsfield API's list price from $0.118/s for five modes up to 1080p; Magnific Draft 480p at 800 credits/4s, 720p at 1,760 credits/4s, and 1080p at 4,400 credits/4s, with annual plan prices of $14.50 / $33.75 / $82.50 per month billed yearly and credits valid for one year; Runway's 20 / 30 / 68 credits per second of output at 480p / 720p / 1080p and $0.01 per credit; fal's roughly $0.2205 / $0.4730 / $1.164 per second estimates; Atlas's standard $0.1397 / $0.3005 / $0.5914 per second estimates at 480p / 720p / 1080p; and the live unlimited windows already stored in the deal data (11.11 sale ending Nov 15, 2026, plus the Business Scale windows with no stated end date).

Confirmed on a vendor page today, but not a catalog row: Atlas estimated SR and ESR modes cited above; Krea's approximate Seedance 2.5 video counts; Higgsfield Plus listing 80 Seedance 2.5 videos on 1,200 credits without a clip length or resolution; Runway's 80-credit minimum, input-video add-on credits, and draft preview billing; fal's and Atlas's token formulas; Magnific credit validity and VAT exclusion.

Unknown: a uniform failed-generation refund rule; minimum top-ups on Higgsfield API, fal, Atlas, Replicate, and Magnific (top-ups are offered on Magnific, but no minimum was stated on the pricing page); whether Higgsfield API's cheapest “from” mode is 480p; a Replicate 1080p rate; a Krea or Higgsfield plan dollars-per-second figure for Seedance 2.5; a public ByteDance self-serve rate. Invented figures are not shown for those gaps.

  • Higgsfield Seedance 2.5 per-clip credits: plan page only says '~80 Seedance 2.5 videos' for 1,200 credits without clip length/resolution (Higgsfield pricing, catalog note). The Plus card rendered on Nov 12, 2026 PT lists 1,200 credits per month and 80 Seedance 2.5 videos, still without clip length or resolution.
  • Krea's pricing page lists approximate Seedance 2.5 video counts (including “Seedance 2.5 5s, 720p, no video reference” and marketing lines such as “~16 Seedance 2.5 videos” on the $9 plan). Those counts are tildes, and the page does not give a single credits-per-clip figure this catalog can convert into dollars per second (Krea pricing, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT).
  • ByteDance's Seedance page does not publish a self-serve dollars-per-second rate (ByteDance Seedance, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT).
  • Replicate lists 480p and 720p only. There is no 1080p rate on the official model page (Replicate Seedance 2.5, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT).
  • Higgsfield API's list says “from $0.118/s” for five modes up to 1080p. The resolution of the cheapest mode is not stated on that list, so that row is not ranked as a 480p, 720p, or 1080p rate. A “Compare with others” table on the same page lists $0.118/s for Text to Video / Image to Video and $0.139/s for Reference to Video / Video Edit / Video Extend, but the table itself says the comparison is based on prices as of 16 September, 2026 (Higgsfield API pricing, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT).

Do credit plans beat the APIs if every credit is used?

At 480p, the cheapest catalog plan rate is $0.132/s on Magnific (Pro (annual)), which is higher than the cheapest catalog API rate of $0.103/s on Replicate. At 720p, the cheapest catalog plan rate is $0.29/s on Magnific (Pro (annual)), which is higher than the cheapest catalog API rate of $0.231/s on Replicate. At 1080p, the cheapest catalog plan rate is $0.726/s on Magnific (Pro (annual)), which is higher than the cheapest catalog API rate of $0.68/s on Runway API. Those plan figures are Magnific annual plans, with credits granted per year and valid for one year. Unused credits raise the effective dollars per second. Higgsfield plan credits for Seedance 2.5 are not turned into a dollars-per-second figure because the plan page does not state clip length and resolution.

Are the unlimited windows the cheapest way?

6 live Higgsfield windows are in the deal data, with clip, resolution, and time caps. They are not $0/s. Break-even seconds below use checkout ÷ the cheapest same-resolution catalog API. The full cap-by-cap comparison is in the Seedance 2.5 unlimited guide. Unlimited Seedance 2.5 plans compared.

How do we calculate this?

Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page (https://vidfare.com/about/).
